answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work; the protocol randomly audits a sample of submissions and forfeits the stake when identities coordinate to claim rewards for nonexistent work. A sybil attacker can create many accounts, but each one needs its own locked capital, and evading audits risks losing it. The pigment on a dune or a willow’s signature can distinguish examples, but neither substitutes for costly accountability.
